faq.q: Which thumbnail sizes can I get, and why is 1280x720 sometimes missing?
faq.a: It probes maxresdefault (1280x720), hqdefault (480x360), mqdefault (320x180), sddefault (640x480), default (120x90), and the three frame grabs (1, 2, 3). maxresdefault only exists if the video was uploaded at 720p or higher, so for older or low-res videos it's genuinely absent and the tool simply won't show it — hqdefault is the always-present fallback.

faq.q: What YouTube link formats are accepted?
faq.a: Standard watch URLs (youtube.com/watch?v=), youtu.be short links, embed URLs, Shorts, live links, the /v/ form, and a bare 11-character video ID. As you type, a live note confirms the detected video ID or warns if you've pasted a channel or playlist link instead of a single video.

faq.q: Can I download several at once?
faq.a: Yes. The Batch Mode tab takes multiple URLs (one per line) and fetches the best available thumbnail for each (maxres if present, otherwise hqdefault), with a Download All button that saves them in sequence. Downloads are fetched as blobs; if CORS blocks a direct download, the image opens in a new tab so you can right-click and save it.

faq.q: Can I use the downloaded thumbnails however I like?
faq.a: No. The tool only accesses the public thumbnail images YouTube already serves — nothing is scraped and no login is used — but the thumbnails remain the copyright of the video's creator. They're fine for personal reference, study, or commentary, but reusing someone else's thumbnail as your own or in advertising isn't permitted.
